chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who arrives from travel during the time of prayer, he said: 'If he does not fear the expiration of the time, let him complete [the prayer]; and if he fears the expiration of the time, let him shorten [it].' And it is possible that the completion refers to one who entered from his travel and the time had entered upon him while he was a traveler, in a manner of recommendation. That which indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What should a traveler do with their prayer if they arrive home during the prayer time?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for a traveler arriving during prayer time, distinguishing between completing the four-rak'ah prayer if time permits and shortening it if time is short. It further suggests that completing the prayer may be a recommended act (istihbab) for one who enters while still technically traveling, reflecting the Shia juristic nuance between the obligation of *qasr* and the permissibility of *tamam*. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the transition from travel to residence status.
